title: Next.js <-> NestJS Communication
outcome: Connect Next.js and NestJS through an explicit, debuggable HTTP boundary with environment-safe base URLs and correct CORS behavior.
artifact: A typed API client boundary that can call the NestJS health/tasks endpoints from the appropriate Next.js execution context.
labSteps: Define API base URLs per environment instead of hard-coding localhost throughout components.
Call a public endpoint from a Server Component and inspect where the request originates.
Call an endpoint from a Client Component and observe browser CORS behavior.
Configure NestJS CORS for the exact development origin and credentials policy required.
Centralize response parsing and non-2xx error handling in one API helper.
Use Network tab plus API logs to trace one failing request end-to-end.
failureModes: Using the browser-only URL from server-to-server code in deployment
Ignoring non-2xx fetch responses because fetch did not throw
Duplicating fetch/error logic in every component
mastery: Can locate a failure on frontend, network, or API side
Can explain CORS as a browser policy
Can build one reusable request helper
principles: Keep the browser dependent on a stable API contract rather than importing backend implementation details.
Configure CORS narrowly for the origins that should call the API.
Centralize base URLs and environment-specific configuration instead of hard-coding localhost throughout components.
Trace failures across browser network tools, API logs, and server responses rather than guessing from UI symptoms.
